newsitem.title: USA: Intelidata sees '97 EPS below forecast.
newsitem.headline: Intelidata sees '97 EPS below forecast.

text.p: InteliData Technologies Corp said on Wednesday it did not expect to meet consensus analysts' earnings expectations for 1997, citing margin pressures caused by product transitions and investments in product development and sales programs.

The First Call consensus earnings estimate for the year was $0.23 per share. In the second quarter, InteliData reported a loss of $0.09 per share versus a loss of $0.20 per share in last year's second quarter.

"Over the next several quarters, as we transition and upgrade our product line from low-end adjuncts to higher-end strategic products, gross margin pressure will continue," Chief Financial Officer John Hillyard said in a statement.
InteliData develops and markets products and services for the telecommunications and financial services industries.
Hillyard said the company also planned to continue its investment in product development and sales and marketing programs for the Intelifone, IPS system and Plexus systems through the rest of 1997.
"As a result, we do not expect to meet the consensus analysts' earnings expectations for 1997," he said.

The company also said its electronic commerce business was still being hurt by two external factors -- delay of the Visa Interactive program and the announcement of a new banking protocol for PC-based software.

The company, which has developed products to support home banking standards offered by Visa, said the Visa Interactive program was stalled due to rumors Visa planned to sell this operation. InteliData said it expected Visa would honor its contractual rights regardless.
Intelidata also said a newly announced software banking protocol delayed sales of its existing products as banks waited for new compatible products.

"While these two events contributed to disappointing first-half results, the outlook for this division should improve once our OFX products are delivered and the Visa Interactive uncertainty is resolved," Chief Executive John Backus said.
